name: USB Grabber Feed
description: Trwały feed video+audio z USB grabbera (MACROSILICON MS2109, /dev/video0) do aplikacji lokalnych przez PipeWire (Ripper USB 0/1) i opcjonalny podgląd okna SDL. Use when you need continuous capture from a USB HDMI grabber for Telegram/Chrome/other PipeWire-aware apps, or to display the feed on the local screen for monitoring. Auto-loads v4l2loopback + gst-launch + pulsesrc command patterns.
workflow: DIAGNOSE: uruchom memphis-probe żeby zweryfikować stan USB, /dev/video*, v4l2loopback, PipeWire sources. Zapisz stan do journal jako 'grabber-feed-baseline'.

VERIFY_MODULE: sprawdź 'lsmod | grep v4l2loopback'. Jeśli brak → potrzebne sudo modprobe v4l2loopback devices=2 video_nr=10,11 card_label="Ripper USB 0","Ripper USB 1" exclusive_caps=0,0 (tier-1, wymaga hasła).
VERIFY_GRABBER: sprawdź 'lsusb | grep 534d'. Jeśli brak → instrukcja operatora (fizyczne podłączenie).
VERIFY_PIPEWIRE: 'wpctl status | grep -A1 Sources' powinien pokazać Ripper USB 0/1 + USB Video. Jeśli brak → restart PipeWire.
TEST_FEED: uruchom memphis-grabber-test (3s test, video+audio entropy). Output JSON z verdict.
DISPLAY_ON_DEMAND: uruchom memphis-display dla podglądu w oknie SDL na lokalnym ekranie.
INSTALL_PERSIST: utwórz systemd user service memphis-grabber-feed.service (tier-1, ale plik tworzony w ~/.config/systemd/user, enable+start bez sudo).
AUDIT: co 24h, memphis_exec + journal wpis 'grabber-feed-audit' z aktualnym stanem.
promptHints: Always run memphis-probe FIRST before any action — get current state from JSON.
v4l2loopback is shared resource — only ONE bridge can write to /dev/video10 at a time. Use 'pgrep -af memphis-bridge' to check for duplicates.
Tier-0 = no sudo: scripts in scripts/ and wrappers in ~/.local/bin/. Tier-1 = sudo one-time: persistent module config + usermod. Never modify src/ without explicit operator approval (tier-2).
Telegram via PipeWire sees /dev/video10 (Ripper USB 0) when bridge is active. Without bridge → 'Ripper USB 0' shows black/freeze. Default is Ripper USB 0 (wpctl set-default 68).
Audio routing is automatic: PipeWire pulsesrc picks up MS2109 USB Audio (ALSA hw:2,0). No config needed for Telegram mic.
Anti-confab phase 6: every figure VERIFIED from JSON output, lsmod, lsusb, wpctl. Never paraphrase counts.

examples.prompt: Uruchom trwały feed z grabbera USB dla Telegram
examples.outcome: Agent runs memphis-probe, memphis-grabber-test, then writes systemd user service memphis-grabber-feed.service, enables it, verifies with systemctl --user status. Records journal 'grabber-feed-baseline' + 'grabber-feed-active'.
Agent runs memphis-display which opens SDL window with video and audio routed to local speakers/headphones.
Agent runs memphis-grabber-test (3s capture, JSON with verdict: DYNAMIC/PARTIAL/STATIC for video, ACTIVE/QUIET/NOISE/SILENT for audio).
Agent runs systemctl --user restart memphis-grabber-feed.service. Verifies with systemctl --user status and journal tail.

notes: Hardened against common pitfalls: module not loaded (sudo needed), grabber unplugged (USB reset), PipeWire stale (restart), bridge duplicate (pgrep first).
All tier-0 scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run.
Audio path: MS2109 USB Audio (card 2) → ALSA → PipeWire pulsesrc → applications. No manual routing.
Telegram Desktop (portable at /home/memphis/Downloads/Telegram/Telegram) is a PipeWire client — uses default source automatically.
